newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rabbi denies charge of groping schoolgirl.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rabbi denies charge of groping schoolgirl.

text.p: A rabbi pleaded not guilty on Tuesday to a federal charge of non-consensual sexual contact following allegations that he groped a 15-year-old girl on a flight from Australia.
Rabbi Israel Grunwald, dressed in the traditional black garb of an ultra-Orthodox Hassidic Jew, denied the charge and said through his lawyer that he spent the flight reading and praying.
The incident occurred on a May 31, 1995 flight from Melbourne, Australia to Los Angeles, when Grunwald was returning from a tour to lecture on morality.
He faces a six-month sentence and a $5,000 fine if convicted.
Grunwald was arrested shortly after landing along with his assistant, Yehudah Friedlander, who has already been sentenced to 22 months in prison for sexually abusing the girl.
According to an FBI affidavit, the girl told authorities both men fondled her on the trans-Pacific flight.

Outside the court, Grunwald's attorney Rex Beaber charged the government had brought the charge for "political reasons" and that he had affidavits from several passengers on the plane saying the assault never happened.
Beaber said the Brooklyn rabbi was so orthodox that his religion prevented him from even shaking hands with a woman.
Assistant U.S. Attorney Debra Yang was asked by Judge James Ideman why it had taken so long to file charges. She replied that she could not reveal the reasons.
Ideman set a hearing for Oct. 28 and said he would give the defence six months to contact witnesses in Australia and bring them to Los Angeles for trial.
